---
title: "Recovery Checkpoint 1: Ready for R"
description: "A short optional recovery route after the MATLAB phase."
---

This checkpoint is for students who missed part of Weeks 1-5 or are unsure
which MATLAB habits must carry into R. It is not an extra assignment unless the
instructor says otherwise.

## Minimum Foundation

Before moving on, you should be able to:

- distinguish a scalar, row vector, column vector, and matrix;
- choose element-wise operations when values should be paired component by component;
- run a saved script from a clean state and interpret an error message;
- describe a function's inputs, outputs, and one boundary test;
- check a plot or numerical result against the original question;
- distinguish interpolation, fitting, and extrapolation;
- explain what residuals reveal;
- record and verify any AI assistance.

## A 45-60 Minute Recovery Route

1. Run the [MATLAB setup check](../code/setup/check_matlab_setup.m).
2. Rerun [the Week 2 function tests](../code/matlab/week02_function_tests.m)
   and explain what each test is protecting against.
3. Complete core Exercises 1 and 2 from [Week 2](week-02-exercises.qmd) and
   Exercise 4 from [Week 3](week-03-exercises.qmd).
4. Write three sentences translating MATLAB habits into neutral language:
   data have shapes, functions have contracts, and results need checks.

## Ready To Continue?

You are ready when you can predict the shape of a short calculation, identify
one useful test before running code, and explain why a visible result is not by
itself proof that the code is correct. If not, bring one specific failed check
to class or office hours.
